title: Restart-channel defect fix: audited fail-closed operator recovery surfaces for HALTED and EMERGENCY_STOPPED + F-2 edge-reachability closure
objective: Close the complete reproduced F-2 defect class per D-024 Amendment 16 (rows D-024-R302..R313): implement an explicit, audited, fail-closed operator recovery surface for the HALTED->IDLE owner_explicit_restart edge; give the EMERGENCY_STOPPED sibling an appropriately STRONGER explicit operator acknowledgment (never automatic or ordinary restart from an emergency stop); enumerate every blocking/terminal state and every recovery edge; prove exactly one documented callable CLI surface per intended operator-recovery edge (intentionally terminal edges explicitly unreachable); add a deterministic removal-sensitive reachability test that fails when a defined recovery edge has no command call site. QUALIFYING EVIDENCE (supervisor-freeze S2/S3): reproduced defect - the owner-typed certified cycle-2 start refused pre-dispatch exit 13 stale_state, illegal transition HALTED->HALTED, because owner_explicit_restart (state_machine.py:399) has zero call sites (project-control/reports/M0-T107-cycle2-start-refusal.md); authorized by D-024-R302. PROHIBITIONS (R310/R311): no generic state-changing command, no manual journal edits, no policy loosening, no budget resets, no audit-history erasure; restart refuses while open asks, pending effects, surviving children, identity drift, or unsafe recovery classification exist. Exactly-once transition + durable audited owner-restart record (R313). Fix invalidates certification and re-triggers R247 (recert = M0-T122).
business_reason: The live limited-auto loop is stranded: after the certified HALT_UNSAFE no documented surface can restart it, so the owner-authorized cycle-2 continuation (Amendment 15) cannot run until this channel exists.
inputs: project-control/reports/M0-T107-cycle2-start-refusal.md (the reproduced defect: root cause + verbatim refusal)

outputs: An explicit, audited, fail-closed operator CLI surface firing HALTED -> IDLE on owner_explicit_restart: exactly one state transition per invocation, a durable audited owner-restart record, refuses under the durable emergency-stop flag and from any other state, clears no flags, resets no budgets, dispatches nothing (R304/R310/R313)

A DISTINCT, appropriately stronger explicit operator acknowledgment surface for EMERGENCY_STOPPED -> IDLE; the ordinary restart surface, every automatic path, and recovery classification refuse it (R305/R306)
Fail-closed restart preconditions: the surface refuses while open asks, pending external effects, surviving children, provider identity drift, or an unsafe recovery classification exist (R311)

Complete enumeration of every blocking/terminal supervisor state and every state-machine recovery edge, with the per-edge proof: exactly one documented callable CLI surface per intended operator-recovery edge; intentionally terminal edges explicitly unreachable (R307/R308, in the producer report)
A deterministic, removal-sensitive reachability test failing whenever a defined recovery edge has no command call site - proven RED on the pre-fix tree, GREEN on the fixed tree (R309)

Test matrix per R312: pre-fix journals (the live journal's shape: HALTED after decision_halt_unsafe, resolved-ask history), current journals, repeated invocation, stale runs, concurrent controllers, emergency-stop recovery, audit-chain continuity, removal sensitivity
Operator documentation updates (README + runbook) for the new surfaces

acceptance_scenarios.scenario: A journal with the LIVE defect shape (HALTED via decision_halt_unsafe, three resolved/denied asks in history, audit chain intact) accepts the new owner-restart command: exactly one HALTED -> IDLE transition on owner_explicit_restart, a durable audited owner-restart record, journal and audit chain remain valid.
acceptance_scenarios.verification: unit test on a reconstructed pre-fix journal; audit-chain continuity asserted before/after

acceptance_scenarios.scenario: Repeated invocation: a second invocation of the restart command refuses cleanly (state is no longer HALTED); no second transition, no journal corruption.

The reachability test enumerates every recovery edge in TRANSITIONS and FAILS on the pre-fix tree (owner_explicit_restart has no call site) and PASSES on the fixed tree; deleting the new command's registration makes it fail again.
acceptance_scenarios.verification: red/green run recorded in the producer report + removal-sensitivity test

acceptance_scenarios.scenario: EMERGENCY_STOPPED: the ordinary restart surface refuses; only the distinct stronger acknowledgment surface exits it; no automatic path (recovery classification, scheduler, succession) can fire either edge.
acceptance_scenarios.verification: unit tests for each refusing path

acceptance_scenarios.scenario: Fail-closed preconditions: with (a) an open ask, (b) a pending external effect, (c) a recorded surviving child, (d) provider identity drift, (e) an unsafe recovery classification, the restart surface refuses with a typed refusal; each precondition individually forces the refusal.
Durable emergency-stop flag set: the HALTED restart surface refuses and directs to the explicit stop-clear discipline first (clear-recovery precedent); no flag is cleared implicitly.

Concurrent controllers / stale runs: with the single-instance lock held elsewhere the command refuses; a stale run identity is surfaced, never silently adopted; state transitions exactly once across racing invocations.
No policy/budget/audit side effects: policy tiers, budgets, counters, and audit history are byte-identical apart from the appended restart records.
